summary: Parkevtate Vosianc's September 22 video asks whether Waste Management is a safe defensive dividend stock to buy now, after management narrowed revenue guidance for the rest of the year while raising its full-year operating-margin forecast on efficiency and cost savings. He highlights Waste Management's appeal as a portfolio diversifier: revenue nearly doubled over the past decade to $25.7B (mix of acquisitions and organic growth plus price increases, with ~5.5% price growth expected this year), the business is barely correlated with the macro economy, and the trailing-12-month operating margin is a solid 18.5%. However, he flags weak capital allocation — trailing ROIC of 8.6%, barely 10% on average over the decade, 'average to below average' by his measure — and notes it is a capital-intensive, not asset-light, business. On valuation, Waste Management now trades at a forward P/E of 23, near the cheaper end of its range (vs over 30 a year ago), reflecting the macro headwinds and lower growth guidance. He revised his DCF modestly higher but expects only modest free-cash-flow growth ($3.8B in 2026 to $4.8B by 2030), giving a $199/share fair value vs a $211 market price — fairly valued on both DCF and forward P/E, which he notes leaves little margin of safety. Nevertheless, given its defensive characteristics and low correlation to the economy, he ranks it a buying opportunity with a favorable risk/reward (low risk, modest reward) — but with low conviction due to valuation and cost headwinds. Calls per supplied list: WM BUY @ $211.
